note: M0.5: the nil/absent LEXICAL divergence. Emacs evaluates the inner form DYNAMICALLY, so the `let' binding of x is gone by the time the captured lambda runs and the funcall raises (void-variable x); the condition-case returns the condition symbol. Fe evaluates lexically by default and ignores the nil LEXICAL argument, so the lambda closes over x=7 and funcall returns 7. This is the case that disproves the old claim that absent/nil `eval' behaves exactly as Emacs.
